title: Partition relations: finite and infinite Ramsey theorems

based_on.title: 580 — III. Partition calculus

summary: Finitely many colours on fixed-size subsets always leave a large set with one colour.
abstract: Suppose every pair, triple, or other fixed-size subset of an infinite set of natural numbers receives one of finitely many colours. Ramsey's theorem guarantees an infinite set whose subsets of that size all have the same colour. A finite version guarantees a set of any prescribed finite size once the original set is sufficiently large. The number of colours must be finite: with countably many colours, pairs can be coloured so that no three-element set has all its pairs the same colour.
